question: When is a contract concluded?
reference: A contract is concluded as soon as two parties exchange two matching expressions of will, subject to any special formalities the law requires for its conclusion [Art. 89].

context.text_en: A contract is created, subject to any special formalities that may be required by law for its conclusion, from the moment that two persons have exchanged two concordant intentions.

context.text_en: If at the time a contract is being framed, an offer is made without a time limit being fixed for acceptance, the offeror is released from his offer if it is not accepted forthwith. question: Can I ask to cancel a contract because I made a fundamental mistake?
reference: Yes. A party who made an essential mistake may ask for the contract to be annulled if the other party made the same mistake, knew of it, or could easily have detected it [Art. 120].

A judgment declaring insolvency renders all debts not yet due by the debtor payable immediately. The agreed or legal interest in respect of the period still to run will be deducted from the debts. The judge may, however, on the petition of the debtor,
